subject: accounting
topic: Company accounts: shares, debentures and reserves

kept.q: What is a debenture in company accounts?
options: A reserve created from retained profits
A loan to a company carrying a fixed rate of interest
A share that carries voting rights
A discount allowed on issue of shares
kept.explanation: A debenture is a form of long-term borrowing by a company. It carries a fixed rate of interest which must be paid whether the company makes profit or not, unlike dividends on shares.
kept.pidgin: Debenture na loan wey company collect, and e dey carry fixed interest rate. Dem must pay the interest even if company no make profit, unlike dividend wey depend on profit.

kept.q: Which of the following is classified as a capital reserve in a company's accounts?
kept.explanation: Share premium arises from capital transactions (issuing shares above nominal value), not from trading profit, so it is a capital reserve. General reserve, retained earnings and dividend equalization reserve are all revenue reserves created from trading profits.
kept.pidgin: Share premium na money wey company collect when e sell shares pass the nominal value, e no come from trading profit, so na capital reserve. The other three na revenue reserves wey come from profit.

kept.q: Afrilink Plc issued 50,000 ordinary shares of ₦2 each at a premium of ₦0.50 per share. All the shares were fully subscribed and paid for. Calculate the total amount received by the company from this issue.
kept.explanation: Each share is sold for the nominal value plus premium: ₦2 + ₦0.50 = ₦2.50. Total received = 50,000 x ₦2.50 = ₦125,000.
kept.pidgin: Each share dem sell am na nominal value plus premium: ₦2 + ₦0.50 = ₦2.50. So total wey company collect na 50,000 x ₦2.50 = ₦125,000.

kept.q: Bayelsa Textiles Ltd has ₦200,000 of 10% debentures in issue. Calculate the amount of annual interest the company must pay to debenture holders.
kept.explanation: Interest on debentures is a fixed percentage of the nominal value of the debentures. 10% of ₦200,000 = ₦20,000 payable yearly regardless of profit level.
kept.pidgin: Debenture interest na fixed percentage of the nominal value. 10% of ₦200,000 = ₦20,000 wey dem go pay every year, profit or no profit.

kept.q: Which of the following correctly describes a key difference between preference shares and ordinary shares?
options: Preference shareholders have priority in dividend payment over ordinary shareholders
Preference shares carry voting rights equal to ordinary shares
Preference share dividend fluctuates with profit exactly like ordinary share dividend
Preference shareholders are paid after ordinary shareholders when the company winds up
kept.explanation: Preference shares usually carry a fixed dividend rate and must be paid before any dividend is given to ordinary shareholders. Ordinary shareholders only receive dividend from what remains, and their dividend varies with profit.
kept.pidgin: Preference shares dey get fixed dividend rate and dem go pay am first before ordinary shareholders. Ordinary shareholders go collect wetin remain, and their own dividend dey change according to profit.

kept.q: A company forfeited 1,000 shares of ₦5 each on which ₦3 per share had been received, including a premium of ₦0.50 per share which had already been fully received before forfeiture. The forfeited shares were later reissued at ₦4 per share, fully paid. Calculate the amount transferred to capital reserve after the reissue.
kept.explanation: Amount forfeited excluding premium = (₦3 - ₦0.50) x 1,000 = ₦2,500. Discount given on reissue = (₦5 - ₦4) x 1,000 = ₦1,000. Balance to capital reserve = ₦2,500 - ₦1,000 = ₦1,500.
kept.pidgin: Amount wey dem forfeit (without premium) = (₦3 - ₦0.50) x 1,000 = ₦2,500. Discount wey dem give for reissue = (₦5 - ₦4) x 1,000 = ₦1,000. Wetin remain go capital reserve = ₦2,500 - ₦1,000 = ₦1,500.

kept.q: Delta Breweries Plc has 20,000 8% preference shares of ₦10 each and 100,000 ordinary shares of ₦5 each. The profit available for distribution is ₦150,000. After paying the preference dividend in full, the directors share the remaining profit equally among the ordinary shares. Calculate the dividend per ordinary share.
kept.explanation: Preference dividend = 8% x ₦10 x 20,000 = ₦16,000. Remaining profit = ₦150,000 - ₦16,000 = ₦134,000. Dividend per ordinary share = ₦134,000 / 100,000 shares = ₦1.34.
kept.pidgin: Preference dividend = 8% x ₦10 x 20,000 = ₦16,000. Wetin remain = ₦150,000 - ₦16,000 = ₦134,000. Dividend for each ordinary share = ₦134,000 / 100,000 = ₦1.34.

kept.q: Which of the following best describes a general reserve in a company's financial statements?
options: Amount received above the nominal value of shares
Profit set aside for unspecified future use, not tied to any particular purpose
Reserve created specifically to redeem debentures
Reserve that can only be used to pay dividends to preference shareholders
kept.explanation: A general reserve is part of retained profit that directors set aside for the overall strengthening of the company, not for any specific named purpose. This makes it different from specific reserves such as a debenture redemption reserve.
kept.pidgin: General reserve na part of profit wey directors set aside to make company strong, e no be for any particular purpose. E different from specific reserve like the one wey dem use to redeem debenture.
